scope: Explicit stock C collation on a native TEXT slot of an ordinary persistent heap table and its use by an index in the same fresh CREATE SCHEMA value.
rules: A native TEXT column may select the absolute stock pg_catalog.C collation. The compiled column records that declared collation separately from its type, literal default and NULL policy.

Non-text storage cannot declare the text collation. Only the exact stock identity is compiled in this domain. Other collation choices and resolving unqualified collation names remain separate full-language obligations.
A plain text column still selects the database default. Field order and the default expression must remain intact when a preceding or following slot declares a stock collation.
A fresh schema composed with a text index binds to its own preceding table slot. An inherited text key selects that declared collation and emits it explicitly in the completed index.
The compiled heap and schema graph contains just declared type, collation, boundaries, downstream key and the other operands used by their effects.
observations: Compare exact ordered field names, storage types and collation identities, defaults and NULL policy, final absolute table and index coordinates, and effective comparison opclasses.
Read pg_attribute, pg_attrdef, pg_collation, and pg_index against the stock native database, and observe typed rows, deterministic order, omitted-default inserts, and failure of required NULL values.
Observe declared stock C separately from the native default on an otherwise comparable neighboring slot. For a fresh schema, verify local ownership despite an external namesake.
negative: A direct non-text declaration carries a stock text collation
An analyzed non-text declaration specifies a collation
A text declaration chooses an out-of-profile collation
A collation placed on a different physical table slot cannot be substituted for the indexed key's collation
faults: Omit the declared column collation when rendering CREATE TABLE
Treat an unresolved column collation as known stock C
Remove the storage-role condition from the column constructor
